recap.back_html: 0 for <pad>, 1 for <unk>. Words start at 2. Build it on training text and save it with the model.
Looks up row i for ID i: (N, L) integer IDs become (N, L, dim). Same as a one-hot vector times the table.
Row 0 starts at zero and gets no gradient, so padding never learns a meaning.
Float IDs raise a dtype error. An ID at or beyond the vocabulary size raises 'index out of range in self'.

snippets: vocab = {"<pad>": 0, "<unk>": 1, "price": 2, "too": 3, "high": 4, "staff": 5, "great": 6}
encode("Price too high", vocab, length=5) # [2, 3, 4, 0, 0]
encode("Staff were great", vocab, length=5) # [5, 1, 6, 0, 0]
lessons.takeaway_html: Build the vocabulary on training text with reserved IDs for padding and unknown words, encode to fixed-length integer IDs, and save the vocabulary with the model.
lessons.title: Tokens, vocabularies and embeddings

recap.back_html: h_t = tanh(x_t @ W_ih.T + h_prev @ W_hh.T + b), with the same weights at every step.
outputs (batch, length, hidden), plus h and c of shape (layers, batch, hidden).
False for RNN and LSTM: (length, batch, features). Wrong layouts often run without error. Set it and assert shapes.
Gradients fade or explode over long sequences (0.9 ** 50 = 0.0052), and steps cannot run in parallel.

snippets: rnn = nn.RNN(input_size=4, hidden_size=8, batch_first=True)
outputs, h_last = rnn(torch.zeros(2, 5, 4)) # (2, 5, 8) and (1, 2, 8)
lessons.takeaway_html: A recurrent network carries a hidden state step by step. Set batch_first=True, and remember its two limits: fading long-range signal and no parallelism.
lessons.title: Sequence models, recurrence and its limits

recap.back_html: weights = softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d)) across keys; output = weights @ V.
Dot products grow like sqrt(d): about 2, 8 and 22 at d = 4, 64, 512. Scaling keeps softmax out of saturation.
Subtract the maximum along the axis with keepdims=True before exp, then divide by the sum along the same axis.
torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v) on (..., length, d) tensors.

snippets: scores = Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(d) # (length, length)
weights = softmax(scores, axis=-1) # each row sums to 1
output = weights @ V # (length, d)
lessons.takeaway_html: Scores are Q @ K.T / sqrt(d), softmax runs across keys with the row maximum subtracted, and the output is the weighted average of the values.
lessons.title: Scaled dot-product attention

recap.back_html: Set masked scores to minus infinity before softmax, so their weights are exactly 0.
np.tril(np.ones((L, L), dtype=bool)): position i sees 0 to i. F.scaled_dot_product_attention(..., is_causal=True) builds it.
scaled_dot_product_attention attn_mask: True = take part. MultiheadAttention key_padding_mask: True = ignore.
Changing a later token, or adding padding, must not change earlier outputs or outputs at real positions.

snippets: scores = np.where(allowed, scores, -np.inf) # allowed: True where attention may look
lessons.takeaway_html: Mask padding and the future by setting their scores to minus infinity. Know which convention each PyTorch function uses, and test that later tokens and padding cannot change earlier outputs.
lessons.title: Masks for padding and for the future

recap.back_html: Project to Q, K, V; split d into h heads of d // h; attend per head; merge and project with Linear(d, d).
4 * d * d + 4 * d, whatever the number of heads. d must divide by num_heads.
Attention ignores order: shuffled inputs give the same outputs, shuffled. Add learned or sinusoidal positions to the embeddings.
PE[pos, 2i] = sin(pos / 10000 ** (2i / d)), PE[pos, 2i + 1] = cos of the same angle.

lessons.takeaway_html: Multi-head attention splits d into heads, attends in each and merges them. Attention ignores order, so add learned or sinusoidal positions to the embeddings.
lessons.title: Multi-head attention and position information

recap.back_html: x = x + attention(norm_1(x)); x = x + feed_forward(norm_2(x)).
Per token: subtract the mean, divide by sqrt(population variance + eps), then a learned scale and shift.
batch_first=False, norm_first=False, dim_feedforward=2048, dropout=0.1. Set the first three yourself.
Mean over real positions only: sum with a 0/1 mask, divide by the count of real tokens.

snippets: x = x + attention(norm_1(x)) # tokens exchange information
x = x + feed_forward(norm_2(x)) # each token is transformed on its own
lessons.takeaway_html: A block is attention then feed-forward, each with layer norm and a residual. Set batch_first, norm_first and dim_feedforward yourself, and pool over real tokens only.
lessons.title: The transformer block, residuals, layer norm and feed-forward

summary: Tokens and embeddings, sequence models, attention, masks, multi-head attention, positions and the transformer block.
title: Attention and transformers from scratch
